items.title: How could Mississauga deal with illegal dumping? A motion would direct staff to study hot spots, prevention options
items.summary: If approved on Sept. 29, city staff will be directed to identify dumping hot spots and evaluate mitigation options and waste bin placement citywide. Furniture is frequently seen dumped around the city, similar to the mattress seen here in Ward 5 of Mississauga in April 2026. A Mississauga councillor is bringing a motion forward to better address illegal dumping and littering across the city. The motion by Ward 5 Coun. Natalie Hart is coming to council for consideration on Sept. 29, and requests staff to study how the city can better keep public spaces, including parks, neighbourhoods and commercial areas, clean. If approved, staff will work to identify hot spots where dumping is a recurring issue and evaluate mitigation options, including changes to operational practices, site design and waste bin placement. The proposal also directs staff to examine public awareness and education initiatives and use of multilingual communications, where possible, to reach the city’s diverse communities with information on proper waste disposal and reporting tools. If approved, staff will also consider potential expansion of the city’s Be A Good Neighbour and neighbourhood standards pilot program which has been running in Ward 5 since August 2025.

items.title: VIA Rail train service eliminated at Mississauga station
items.summary: In a move intended to “improve overall travel times,” VIA Rail says it’s eliminating train service at a station in the north end of Mississauga starting late next month. The Crown corporation and Canada’s lone national passenger train operator says effective Oct. 25, “we will no longer serve or stop” at the Malton station, which is located on Derry Road East. Cutting VIA Rail train service in Malton will help “improve overall travel times,” the national operator said. ” The move comes as part of VIA Rail’s latest schedule review, which was announced in mid-September and initially called for all service to Guildwood station in Toronto (Scarborough) to be permanently cut as well. However, backlash from commuters and others in that part of Toronto forced VIA Rail to reconsider its decision this past Friday. As a result, the trains will continue to serve the Scarborough station — VIA’s only depot in that part of Toronto — beyond Oct. 25 as the train operator launches its winter schedule. VIA Rail is also adjusting other services in its Quebec City-to-Windsor corridor as part of its schedule review, conducted twice a year. “The revised schedule will better align service with passenger demand, strengthen network resilience and support more reliable and predictable service,” VIA Rail said in a September news release. ” Saturday service on trains 68 and 69 will be replaced by new departures on trains 668 and 669, VIA Rail said.

items.title: National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
items.summary: This week’s article is born through gathering, and sharing, information on local, provincial and national observations for the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation. September 30th marks both the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation and Orange Shirt Day (Every Child Matters). The 2026 observance continues Canada’s commitment to acknowledging the harms of residential schools and advancing reconciliation through education, remembrance, and community participation. The day serves as a powerful reminder of the lasting impacts of the Residential School system. What began as a grassroots initiative has since evolved into a nationally recognized movement, with individuals, organizations, and communities across Canada participating in acts of remembrance, reflection, and reconciliation each year. Public commemoration of this tragic chapter in Canada’s history, and its lasting effects, plays an essential role in advancing truth and reconciliation. TRUTH AND RECONCILIATION, 2024, CITY OF MISSISSAUGA. The National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, established in 2021, recognizes Survivors, their families, and communities while ensuring the history and legacy of residential schools are publicly remembered. On September 30, Canadians are encouraged to wear orange in honour of Residential School Survivors and their families, and in remembrance of the children who never returned home. There are many ways to pause and reflect on Truth and Reconciliation: Illuminating Parliament Hill: to commemorate the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation the Peace Tower and the Senate Building in Ottawa will be illuminated in orange throughout the evening of September 30. National Commemorative Gathering: APTN and the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation invite Canadians to take part in the National Commemorative Gathering: Remembering the Children – National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.

items.title: High-Risk Ontarians Can Get Free Flu and COVID Shots Starting Today, With Wider Rollout Next Month
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, Ontario has begun rolling out free flu and COVID-19 vaccines this week, starting with high-risk groups before opening to the general public next month. Hospital staff and patients, residents and staff at long-term care and retirement homes, and people in other congregate living settings can get the shots immediately, along with anyone 65 and older. The province says most other residents will have to wait until Oct. 26 for their turn, while infant RSV immunization is set to begin Oct. 1. Availability may vary between individual pharmacies and health care providers even within the eligible groups. The vaccines are meant to reduce the spread of serious flu and COVID-19 symptoms heading into the colder months. The Government of Canada notes that flu symptoms typically appear one to four days after exposure, and can include fever, cough, muscle aches, chills, fatigue, sore throat and a stuffy nose. Left untreated, the flu can worsen existing chronic conditions and lead to pneumonia, heart complications or respiratory failure requiring hospitalization. Federal data cited in the report puts the flu among the top ten causes of death in Canada, linked to roughly 3,500 deaths a year.

items.title: Credit River Salmon Begin Their Annual Push Upstream From Lake Ontario
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the annual salmon run is underway along the Credit River as thousands of fish leave Lake Ontario each fall to swim upstream and spawn. The migration typically begins in September, peaks in early October and continues through the fall depending on weather and water conditions. Guided by instinct, the salmon return to the same waters where they hatched, battling strong currents along the way. Once they reach calmer water, they dig a gravel nest called a redd, where they lay their eggs before their life cycle ends. The city calls it one of Mississauga's most remarkable wildlife events, drawing residents to local parks and trails each year to watch the fish fight their way home. Officials are asking anyone heading out to observe the run to do so respectfully and let the salmon complete a journey they have spent years preparing for.

items.title: Charge up your fire safety knowledge this Fire Prevention Week
items.summary: Learn how simple charging habits can help prevent fires and keep your home and family safe. Emergency and public safety | September 28, 2026 Every October, Fire Prevention Week is a reminder that fire safety starts with simple actions at home. From October 4 to 10, Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services (MFES) is encouraging residents to learn how safe device charging habits can help prevent fires and keep homes, families and communities safe. Meet MFES members at various locations in the city during the week to learn about fire safety. Fire Prevention Week is an annual public education campaign that helps people learn how to prevent fires and stay safe in an emergency. Observed across North America, it provides an opportunity for residents to refresh their fire safety knowledge, review emergency plans and learn about fire risks that affect homes and communities today. This year’s Fire Prevention Week theme, “Charge Into Fire Safety: Safe Charging Is a Superpower,” focuses on the everyday charging habits that can reduce the risk of fires caused by lithium-ion batteries. These batteries are found in many devices people use every day including cell phones, laptops, tablets, e-bikes, e-scooters and power tools. They store a large amount of energy in a small space and can become dangerous if they are damaged, used incorrectly or charged improperly. The theme reflects a growing concern for fire services across North America. As rechargeable batteries become more common in homes, workplaces and transportation devices, fire departments are responding to more incidents involving lithium-ion batteries. MFES has identified lithium-ion batteries as the city’s fastest-growing ignition source, recording a 122 per cent increase in lithium-ion battery-related fires in 2025 compared to the year before. These fires can start suddenly, spread quickly and are often difficult to extinguish.

items.title: Provincial Funding Boost for Peel Police Follows Steep Drop in Local Auto Thefts
items.summary: According to Insauga and CBC Toronto, Peel Regional Police auto theft numbers have kept falling, dropping from 3,089 vehicles stolen between January and June of 2025 to 2,790 over the same six months this year. Peel police Chief Nishan Duraiappah said the force has made real progress but wants to keep the pressure on organized crime groups behind the thefts. The comments came as Ontario Solicitor General Michael Kerzner visited Peel police headquarters in Mississauga on Monday to announce part of a new $6 million provincial commitment to fighting auto theft, with $300,000 of that earmarked for Peel police specifically. Kerzner credited the funding and added police resources for the province wide decline, while cautioning that the fight is not over. Data from Equite Association's 2025 auto theft trend report shows vehicle thefts across Ontario fell to 19,319 last year, down 36 percent from a peak of 30,134 in 2023.

items.title: This free tool allows voters in 50 Ontario municipalities to compare their views with election candidate positions
items.summary: We’ve partnered with Vox Pop Labs to launch Vote Compass, a free, easy-to-use tool that provides voters an opportunity to compare their views with those of local candidates looking to represent them in the Oct. 26 municipal election. Vote Compass is a free, easy-to-use tool developed to help voters see how their views on local issues align with those of candidates vying for their vote in the Oct. 26 municipal election. The municipal election is just around the corner. items.title: Mississauga Library Pitches Its Free Card as One of the City's Best Money-Saving Tools
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a free library card is being promoted as one of the most valuable items residents can carry in their wallet as living costs continue to climb. Mississauga Library says the card unlocks far more than book borrowing, including movies, video games, online learning courses, career resources and family programming that would otherwise require paid subscriptions. Thousands of digital titles are available to borrow anytime through the library's online collection, alongside access to magazines, newspapers and other trusted news sources from around the world. The library frames itself as more than a lending service, describing its branches as community spaces where people can learn new skills, attend events and build connections regardless of age, income or background. Officials are encouraging residents who have not signed up to get a card and explore what the system offers, from career support to language learning resources.
